Erdős problem #257

Reciprocal sums over infinite exponent supports

Is the sum of 1/(2𝑛 −1)1/(2n−1) over every infinite set of positive exponents irrational?

Open Problem on GitHub

Results and open questions

#257. Fix a finite nonempty set of primes 𝑃P and let ℎ(𝑎)h(a) be the largest divisor of 𝑎a supported on 𝑃P. For an infinite support 𝐴A and an integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, finiteness of ∑𝑎∈𝐴ℎ(𝑎)/(𝑎(𝑏ℎ(𝑎) −1))∑a∈Ah(a)/(a(bh(a)−1)) implies irrationality of ∑𝑎∈𝐴1/(𝑏𝑎 −1)∑a∈A1/(ba−1). The long paper explains the proof: average the residues along multiples of increasingly divisible moduli, then choose a finite range of averaging lengths to control the error uniformly. Lean proves this as divisibilityWeightedClaim in WeightedReturn.lean. The short paper gives a shorter proof and an explicit support with divergent reciprocal sum satisfying the criterion.

The comparison is with Erdős’s earlier reciprocal-summable condition, which he stated for every integer base after proving the pairwise-coprime case. For 𝑃 ={2}P={2}, write 𝑎 =2𝑘𝑚a=2km with 𝑚m odd: the weighted summand is 1/[𝑚(𝑏2𝑘 −1)]1/[m(b2k−1)]. In the short paper’s example A★ = {2^k m : k ≥ 1, m odd, m ≤ 2^{2^k}}, dyadic blocks show that the odd reciprocals in the 𝑘kth layer sum to between 2𝑘/42k/4 and 2𝑘2k. The layer therefore contributes at least 1/41/4 to ∑_{a∈A★} 1/a, but at most 21−𝑘21−k to the base-two weighted sum. The ordinary reciprocal sum diverges while the weighted sum converges.

The theorem gives irrationality at every integer base for every infinite subset of A★. It does not cover full support, all odd exponents, or the full prime support; Tao–Teräväinen prove the latter at base two by another method. The comparison identifies the added class and proof mechanism, but does not settle independent novelty or priority assessment. See the short paper’s theorem, example and sources. At base two, the weighted condition can also be combined with the positive divisor-cover criterion: the long paper proves that a common finite averaging window makes both displacements small.

Every infinite subset of their union then has irrational subseries at every integer base. Lean proves this as mixedSupportClaim in the same module. Neither theorem establishes the separately proposed hosts separating the two classes. Every infinite reciprocal-summable support satisfies it, yielding the coprimality-free extension stated by Erdős. Full-support irrationality at every integer base is classical (Erdős 1948) and Lean-checked here, as are pairwise-coprime summable-reciprocal support and Lebesgue measure one for the base-2 achievement set. Irrationality for every infinite support and the 1/21/2 and 1/211/21 branches remain open.

The weighted theorem is Lean-checked. The exact five-declaration PalomarCorpus/E257_01 entry, which includes divisibilityWeightedClaim, passed Palomar mechanical verification for source commit b85ed30805188eb4390a686b111294b24363418e. Palomar accepted a registration request for submission gid0ym5uu910 at 19:31 UTC on 24 September 2026. At the authenticated status check at 19:42 UTC, no public ID or version had been returned. Its verification covers the selected interface, not every claim in the paper or the unrestricted Erdős problem. Read the short paper, long record, and separate Comparator verification status.

Read the public result guide

Check the 189/388 example

This exact-rational calculation concerns one proposed member of the Mersenne achievement set. It does not test the weighted irrationality theorem above or settle the universal Problem 257.

From the mathematics repository root, run the exact-rational script with Python 3:

python3 research/experiments/sparse_interpolation/late_rejection.py

Saved output excerpt from that script (the page itself does not run a check):

target: 189/388
first_rejection: 17
tail_upper_bound: 196609/25769803776
remainder: 9291822600689/1217890317075045460
weight: 1/131071

At step 17, the exact inequality is tail upper bound < remainder < current weight. Earlier greedy choices are certified, so this particular rational cannot be represented as a subsum of 1/(2^n−1). The script also checks 577/388 and a separate finite factorial calculation. Read the explanation and limits.

Continue with a broader finite probe

python3 research/experiments/choices_contraction/rational_membership_probe.py --hosts all --q 12 --depth 10 --horizon 80

This second script reports excluded when it finds a finite certificate, finite representation when it reaches zero, or not excluded through depth 10 when neither occurs in this run. Survival at finite depth does not prove membership. Read its method and saved results.

The example following the proof in Section 3 makes this precise. The reciprocal mass at each fixed 𝑃P-part must be finite, and its weighted sum over the parts must converge; the first requirement alone is insufficient. Section 1.2 of the companion, Reciprocal Mersenne Subseries, gives the decomposition and a separating example.

The full set of primes fails too, since the primes outside 𝑃P contribute 1/[𝑎(𝑏 −1)]1/[a(b−1)]. These are limitations of this criterion, not assertions of rationality. By contrast, ℎ/(2ℎ −1) ≤1h/(2h−1)≤1 shows that it includes every reciprocal-summable support.

Theorem 1.2 (reciprocal-summable supports). Let 𝐴 ⊆ℕ>0A⊆N>0 be infinite. If

Erdős stated Theorem 1.2, including the all-base conclusion, after proving its pairwise-coprime case . We give a complete averaging proof of that stated extension. Erdős also discussed weakening reciprocal summability [7]; no identification of the weighted condition with his suggested conditions is asserted.

The order of limits is essential: the observation length tends to infinity with the modulus fixed, and only then does the modulus increase. Reciprocal summability controls both interchanges.

Extensions beyond reciprocal summability

The weighted condition can hold when ∑𝑎∈𝐴1/𝑎∑a∈A1/a diverges, so the previous proof’s summable majorant is no longer available. We instead bound finite averages for each exponent and then average over dyadic observation lengths. This second average controls the incomplete periods. Estimate (S) will also allow the divisor-cover argument to use these same observation lengths.

Both proofs select a term no larger than a finite average. For a related selection step on arithmetic progressions, see Duverney–Tachiya [1]. A counterexample and the distinct bound for ordinary initial intervals are proved in the companion, Section 13; those proofs were first worked out in an AI-assisted note of 17 September 2026. The three results of that section also have Lean proofs, each compared independently by Comparator; the ordinary proofs have not had independent human review. Those arguments concern finite functionals, not a comparison of the infinite-support irrationality classes. No separation between the weighted supports of Theorem 1.1 and the cover supports of Theorem 3.1 is proved here.

Overlaps between the supports only improve the inequality. Infinitude of 𝐴A makes its displacement positive. The atom comparison used in the cover proof transfers arbitrarily small displacements to every integer base; the fixed rational lattice then excludes rationality. ◻

The proof does not establish strict containment of either individual class in the mixed class.

With arbitrary positive cover weights, the class of subsets of such mixed hosts is closed under finite unions and finite changes. For weighted supports use the union of the two finite prime sets: the prime part grows and ℎ/(2ℎ −1)h/(2h−1) decreases. For two covers, interleave their finite sets with weights 𝜂𝑗/2ηj/2 and 𝜃𝑗/2θj/2; the total cost grows by at most two, since 2𝛼𝑗 ≤22αj≤2. Subsets inherit the same hosts, and finite sets have finite weighted mass. This argument uses the positive-weight variant; it does not silently reindex the dyadic weights in (V). Countable unions require a tail budget. Every prime singleton is admitted, but for the full prime support PP one has Δ2,P(𝑁) >1/3Δ2,P(N)>1/3 for every 𝑁 ≥1N≥1: indeed ∑𝑟≥12−𝑟𝜔(𝑁 +𝑟) ≥1∑r≥12−rω(N+r)≥1, whereas 𝑋P(2) ≤∑𝑎≥2(2𝑎 −1)−1 <2/3XP(2)≤∑a≥2(2a−1)−1<2/3. Here 𝜔(𝑛)ω(n) is the number of distinct prime divisors of 𝑛n. The reciprocal-summable class is contained in the weighted class, since ℎ/(2ℎ −1) ≤1h/(2h−1)≤1. Theorem 1.2 supplies the direct proof of that baseline case.

For comparison, Tao–Teräväinen prove the full-prime case at base 22 [3]. The paragraph following it states extensions to prime support at every integer base and to full prime-power support at base 22, leaving the modifications to the reader. It does not treat arbitrary infinite thinnings. The proposed thinning extension is not a premise of any theorem here.

𝑋{2,3}(2)=1021,𝑋{2,6}(2)=2263.X{2,3}(2)=1021,X{2,6}(2)=2263.

By contrast, Van Assche constructs approximants for the full Lambert series and proves both nonvanishing and decay of the associated integer linear forms . That approximation mechanism does not follow from denominator survival alone.

Limits of the small-displacement criterion

The preceding criteria establish irrationality by making Δ2,𝐴(𝑁)Δ2,A(N) positive and arbitrarily small. The particular requirement inf𝑁≥1Δ2,𝐴(𝑁) =0infN≥1Δ2,A(N)=0 fails at full support:

Δ2,ℕ>0(𝑁)>(2𝑁−1)∑𝑎>𝑁2−𝑎=1−2−𝑁≥12(𝑁≥1).Δ2,N>0(N)>(2N−1)∑a>N2−a=1−2−N≥12(N≥1).

The full-support value is nevertheless irrational . Thus a proof covering full support cannot rely solely on this small-displacement requirement. This does not exclude other integer linear forms or other uses of averaging.

The distinction also appears in the squarefree support. Its series is irrational at every base 2𝑗2j, 𝑗 ≥1j≥1, by Corollary 1.2 and Example 1.1 of Duverney and Tachiya [1]. Their corollary covers the 𝑠s-free products of any pairwise coprime sequence of polynomial growth, and they present it as support for the conjecture of Erdős and Graham stated here as Problem 1.3. The zero-window obstruction for one normalised certificate scheme concerns that scheme’s hypotheses. It gives no obstruction to irrationality of the value. The precise normalisation counterexamples are retained in the companion, together with the complete catalogue of known support families.

A growth-only criterion gives a different class: if 𝐴 ={𝑐1 <𝑐2 <⋯}A={c1<c2<⋯} and lim sup𝑛𝑐𝑛/2𝑛 =∞lim supncn/2n=∞, then 𝑋𝐴(𝑏)XA(b) is irrational for every integer 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 [8]. The companion, Section 1.7, proves the translation from denominator growth and gives examples showing that this class and reciprocal summability are incomparable. The interval-filling constructions in [9] and the freely chosen lacunary denominators of [16] are not constructions of subseries of these fixed Mersenne weights.

Prime-incidence arguments require additional care as well: multiplying all prime exponents by 22 creates positive correlations between their divisibility indicators. The exact identity and covariance calculation are in the companion, Section 1.5. Size conditions alone do not supply that independence.

Further questions

The support theorems give sufficient conditions for irrationality; the tests below instead concern whether a specified rational is a subseries sum. Their hypotheses must be verified for the actual selector or for finite approximants at arbitrarily large depths. An equivalent test does not itself establish membership.

The finite uniqueness statement is also explicit: if 𝐷 ⊆{2,…,𝑅}D⊆{2,…,R} and an integer 𝑠s satisfy ∑𝑑∈𝐷𝑞2𝑅(𝑑) +𝑠 =𝑇2𝑅∑d∈Dq2R(d)+s=T2R with 0 ≤𝑠 ≤2𝑅0≤s≤2R, then 𝐷 =𝐷𝑅D=DR and 𝑠 =𝑠𝑅s=sR. This is the denominator-specific separation theorem (uniqueness of a finite representation with the stated remainder bound). The cited finite crossing lemmas give additional consequences under their alignment hypotheses: an earlier finite prefix cannot occur, and a real greedy exponent must be skipped (the missing-prefix consequence of an aligned crossing, the real greedy skip forced by that crossing).

Compactness proves the implication; it does not produce the approximating supports.

Theorem 9.3 (unbounded shared-prefix families imply a half-support). Suppose that for every 𝑁N there are 𝑀,𝐾M,K with max{𝑁,1} ≤𝑀max{N,1}≤M, 0 ≤𝐾 ≤𝑀0≤K≤M, and a family satisfying all the conditions in the preceding paragraph. Then 𝑋𝐴(2) =1/2XA(2)=1/2 for some infinite set 𝐴 ⊆ℕ>0A⊆N>0.

Choosing one member from each family gives the terminal bound in Theorem 9.2, proving the conclusion. The shared-prefix conditions are needed for the proposed construction of the families, not for this final compactness step. Such a construction at unbounded depths would refute Problem 1.3; none is proved here.

Sources

Erdős’s five-page paper was checked directly: p. 222 states the reciprocal-summable extension without proof, and p. 226 describes the fractional-part approach. The original Luca–Tachiya and Hornich articles were not independently retrieved. The periodic theorem was checked in Luca and Tachiya’s own account [11], and the strict-tail result in Nitecki’s exposition. The Formal Conjectures file  is statement-level prior art, not a proof dependency.

The evidence record lists the Lean declarations behind each marked result, with their versions and independent checks. The Lean sources for the supplementary statements quoted from the companion (finite sums and denominators, the achievement set and its restrictions, squarefree divisor counts, half-membership and the tests for 1/211/21) are linked beside the corresponding statements there.

Library declarations.

Several statements of this note and its companion rest on the following library declarations, each opened at a fixed revision. Pairwise-coprime supports: factorial-support instance; powers-of-two-support instance; pairwise-coprime theorem. Eventually periodic weights: irrationality for the stated eventually periodic weights. Fixed-core supports: carry certificates for the stated fixed-core support; irrationality for the stated fixed-core support. Finite supports and denominators: noncollapse for the reduced rational denominator. Rational values and carries: rational support values and Möbius-inverted carries; rationality and integer recurrences with vanishing scaled error; a lower bound for reciprocal mass; unboundedness of the shifted odd-tail recurrence; lengths of intervals with zero divisor count. Composite dilation: the divisor-count identity under dilation; the upper bound for the dilation correction; the example with exponents two and six. The achievement set: Lebesgue measure one; perfect; totally disconnected; nowhere dense; membership and greedy tail bounds; non-membership of 3/43/4; the greedy form; the finite-support exclusion. Restricted achievement sets: the formal dichotomy. Greedy skips and exact rows: the cofinal-skip hypothesis; an exact finite sum from one greedy skip; exact finite sums from arbitrarily late greedy skips; membership from infinitely many greedy skips; the upper-half Boolean fill. Membership of 1/21/2: the terminal-bit form; the skipped-rank form. The two-thirds band: general band localization; two-thirds band; integral safety; odd numerator bound.

What is checked in Lean
  • Irrationality at every integer base for the classical full support, reciprocal-summable supports, and the finite-prime weighted supports in divisibilityWeightedClaim.
  • Every infinite subset of the union of a finite base-two weighted-mass host and a strengthened positive-cover host has irrational series at every integer base (mixedSupportClaim).
  • Unique Mersenne coding on every support; compactness and nowhere density; perfection for infinite support; finite-complement measure 2−|𝐹|2−|F|, otherwise zero.
What is not checked
  • Universal irrationality over all infinite supports, or the proposed rational values 1/21/2 and 1/211/21.
  • Fair-bit laws, finer singularity results, and periodic-stride dimensions.
  • Any bridge from geometric uniqueness or measure rigidity to arithmetic irrationality.
The formal record: 15 main results, 2 open obligations, 1 Lean module, Comparator review

Main results

Statements and boundaries are copied from the corpus record. Registry status: programme_only

mixed prior-art geometry and locally proved metric result; novelty unassessed family: achievement_set_geometry

The base-2 Mersenne achievement set has Lebesgue measure exactly one.

This does not decide whether every infinite-support sum is irrational.

Erdos249257.volume_mersenneAchievementSet
formalisation of an existing theorem family: known_irrational_supports

For every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, the full-support Erdos-Borwein series is irrational.

This is the classical full-support theorem, not universal Erdos #257.

Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSum_full_support
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: finite_prime_weighted_support

For every base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, an infinite positive support A with finite prime-weighted mass in base b has irrational support series; if a positive host H has finite prime-weighted mass in base 2, every infinite subset of H has irrational support series at every base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2.

The finite-prime weighted-summability premise is explicit in both clauses. This criterion does not cover every infinite support or settle universal Erdős #257; no novelty, priority, significance, or external human-review claim is made.

ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.divisibilityWeightedClaim
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: finite_prime_weighted_support

For every base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2, if a positive host H has finite prime-weighted mass in base b, every infinite subset A of H has irrational support series in the same base b.

This hereditary result retains the same-base weighted-summability hypothesis; it does not infer all-base irrationality from weighted mass at an arbitrary base, or settle universal Erdős #257.

ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.finitePrimeWeighted_fixedBase_hereditary
formalisation of an existing theorem family: pairwise_coprime_support

For every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 and every infinite pairwise-coprime support A with summable reciprocal mass, the support-restricted Mersenne series is irrational.

This is the pairwise-coprime support theorem, not universal Erdos #257; the infinitude, pairwise-coprimality, and summable-reciprocal hypotheses remain explicit.

Erdos249257.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_pairwise_coprime
formalised here; novelty unassessed family: periodic_nonnegative_weight_irrationality

For every integer base 𝑏 ≥2b≥2 and every eventually-periodic nonnegative rational coefficient sequence γ with a positive value at a positive index in its periodic region, the series ∑𝑎𝛾(𝑎)/(𝑏𝑎 −1)∑aγ(a)/(ba−1) is irrational.

This is the nonnegative rational eventually-periodic coefficient theorem; its nonnegativity, eventual periodicity, and positive-tail hypotheses remain explicit, and the broader mixed-sign periodic theorem is not claimed.

Erdos249257.irrational_ratWeightSeries_eventuallyPeriodic
conditional reduction; novelty unassessed family: orthogonal_petal_sunflower_reduction

For every support A carrying the finite-core OrthogonalPetalBouquet structure and satisfying the exact uniform SunflowerForcedSlotTailSelection predicate, the base-2 support-restricted Mersenne series erdosSupportSeries 2 A is irrational.

This is a conditional reduction: the bouquet structure and uniform tail-selection predicate remain hypotheses; neither is constructed for arbitrary supports, so this does not add an unconditional Erdos #257 support family or solve the universal problem.

Erdos249257.SupportSunflowerDichotomy.irrational_erdosSupportSeries_of_orthogonalPetalBouquet
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: finite_period_noncollapse

For a reduced finite Mersenne sum, the base order modulo the denominator equals the support lcm.

The finite-support theorem does not settle any infinite-support sum.

Erdos249257.finite_period_noncollapse_rat_den
locally proved result; novelty unassessed family: restricted_achievement_sets

A support-restricted Mersenne achievement set has exact finite-complement measure or measure zero for infinite complement.

The measure dichotomy does not classify rational points.

ErdosProblems.Erdos257.volume_supportedMersenneAchievementSet_dichotomy
conditional reduction family: shifted_odd_tail_state

A rational support value with a positive support seed and denominator 2𝑐 ∗𝑣2c∗v produces a positive natural shifted tail state with an exact binary recurrence and a modular doubling orbit modulo v.

This state-extraction theorem does not exclude rational infinite supports or settle universal Erdős #257; the support and rational-value hypotheses remain explicit.

Erdos249257.exists_shifted_odd_tail_nat_states_of_support_fraction
locally proved exact equivalence plus conditional consequences; novelty unassessed family: boolean_mobius_carry

For p : ℤ and 𝑞 >0q>0, a nonempty positive-index support with erdosSupportSeries 2 𝐴 =A= p/q exists exactly when a quotient-only Boolean–Möbius carry certificate exists, with positive square-root-bounded integer orbit, divisible carry differences, and support reconstructed from its Boolean Möbius transform.

The equivalence is stated at the existence level with 𝑞 >0q>0, 0 ∉ A, and a positive support witness; it gives no contradiction, no universal Erdős #257 irrationality result, and no producer of cofinally nonintegral shifts for the actual recurrence. The generic tempered-orbit theorem and the reciprocal-mass, unbounded-tail, and zero-window results are subordinate consequences, not separate families; the zero-window constant depends on the support and numerator and is not uniform. This does not settle every infinite support, and no novelty, priority, significance, external-review, or unrestricted #257 endpoint claim is made.

Erdos249257.exists_normalized_support_fraction_iff_exists_booleanMobiusCarry
conditional reduction; novelty unassessed family: boolean_mobius_exact_row_dynamics

If positive rational-greedy skips occur cofinally in the declared sense, the skipped-core construction supplies cofinally many exact local Mersenne half rows and hence (1 / 2 : ℝ) belongs to the Mersenne achievement set.

This route is conditional on the unproved CofinalPositiveHalfGreedySkips premise: for every N there is 𝑐 ≥maxc≥max N 4 with a positive greedy remainder below mersenneWeightRat c. A finite exact row or any finite collection of exact rows does not establish that cofinal supply. The result is a conditional 1/2-membership/counterexample route only, not an unconditional solution of Erdős #257; the exact-row, upper-half Boolean-word, rank-two, and endpoint-defect declarations are subordinate mechanism evidence, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_of_positiveHalfGreedySkips
locally proved exact endpoint classification; novelty unassessed family: half_membership_seam_classification

Membership of 1/21/2 in the Mersenne achievement set is equivalent to unbounded false successor terminal bits, equivalently to an unbounded upper-or-middle successor branch, cofinal terminal-false positions, unbounded skipped ranks along the integer seam, infinite greedy skipped support, and no last half-greedy skip.

This exact endpoint-socket classification does not supply any unbounded terminal-false or upper-or-middle occurrences, cofinal supply, skipped-support producer, or half-membership witness; finite exact rows do not establish the required global supply. It is not an unconditional or universal Erdős #257 result, and no novelty, priority, significance, or external-review claim is made.

Erdos249257.half_mem_mersenneAchievementSet_iff_unboundedTerminalFalse
unconditional progress family: composite_dilation_defect_identity

For a positive support element a and positive x, the divisor-count coefficient at a*x splits into the coefficient at x, the distinguished new divisor when a does not divide x, and an exact finite composite-dilation defect.

The exact defect is not bounded for arbitrary supports and supplies no tail selector or irrationality theorem; the separate bouquet budget remains conditional on its structural hypotheses.

Erdos249257.CompositeDilationDefect.supportCoeff_mul_eq_add_defect
no-go result family: half_and_twenty_one_frontiers

For positive odd integers p, D, and q, the integer form of the two-thirds band forces 𝑝 ≥7p≥7; the small odd numerator classes 1, 3, and 5 are therefore excluded.

This is local 2-adic band arithmetic: 𝑝 =7p=7 is sharp for the stated hypotheses, and the theorem does not prove that an actual half-greedy orbit reaches or avoids the band, nor does it prove half-membership.

Erdos249257.HalfGreedyTwoThirdsBand.seven_le_of_intBand_odd

Open obligations

Prove any one of these and the corresponding reduction above becomes unconditional.

  • arithmetic_rigidity_for_thin_supports Convert hereditary unique coding into an arithmetic obstruction to rational values for every infinite support, including zero-measure Cantor supports.
  • formalise_measure_and_stride_geometry Extend the measure dichotomy to Bernoulli laws and periodic-stride dimensions without implying arithmetic consequences.
